meta.title: From Compliance to Conviction — Bank Muamalat and the Shariah-Authenticity Question
meta.analyst: i-ARIF (Hermes edge bridge) — computational output under F13 sovereign direction

epistemic_key.OBS: directly observed in a cited primary/secondary source
epistemic_key.FIQH: a matter of religious ruling — authority rests with qualified scholars, not with this analysis

authenticity_gap.debt_based_note: commodity murabahah / tawarruq estimated at 'almost 90% or more' of the Islamic banking sector
authenticity_gap.pls_share_narrow_note: musharakah 0.23-0.71% + mudharabah 0.12-0.40% of total financing (Malaysia, working-paper series)
authenticity_gap.pls_share_alt_note: PLS financing ~0.5% of total financing in Malaysia (Chong & Liu 2009; Nor & Ismail 2020)
authenticity_gap.pls_share_broad_note: broader definition: PLS contributes up to 10-15% of total Islamic financing in Malaysia

bmmb.book_composition_note: FY2024 home financing 33.51% of gross financing; personal financing 28.6% (Mar 2024 disclosure). Home and Ar Rahnu both structured on tawarruq.
bmmb.gabv_note: First Islamic bank in the world and first bank in Southeast Asia to join the Global Alliance for Banking on Values
bmmb.gold_i_account: Gold-i account with automatic zakat deduction on haul and nisab
bmmb.atlas_digital: Atlas — digital-only Islamic banking platform launched 2026

capital_sensitivity.pls_rw_note: Literature reports musharakah and mudarabah exposures attracting materially higher capital risk weights (up to 400%) than debt-based financing — the structural capital penalty on risk-sharing.

regulatory.bnm_ar2025: Islamic financing rose to 48% of total financing; takaful participation 24.5%. BNM states activities with longer horizons and unpredictable cashflows 'cannot rely on traditional debt alone' and launched i-CITA to promote wider use of mudarabah and musyarakah.
regulatory.ifsb_ifsr_2026: Released 26 May 2026 — 'Emergence of Hybrid Risks in Islamic Banking'. Notes new products and balance-sheet configurations 'increasingly mimic conventional banking characteristics' and may not be captured by existing prudential frameworks.
regulatory.ifsb_bangladesh: The IFSB 2026 report documents an Islamic banking crisis rooted in 'systematic concentration of ownership: a single business group acquired controlling stakes in five of ten full-fledged Islamic banks through multiple entities under common control.'
regulatory.kl_declaration: The Kuala Lumpur Declaration holds risk-sharing to be a salient characteristic of Islamic financial transactions, and asserts the principle that liability is inseparable from the right to profit.
regulatory.oic_fiqh_academy_2003: 17th session — organised and reverse tawarruq regarded as impermissible.
regulatory.bnm_sac: BNM's Shariah Advisory Council accepts organised tawarruq subject to specific rules and parameters (Tawarruq policy document, reissued December 2018).
regulatory.divergence_note: The Malaysian SAC framework accepts structures that AAOIFI and Gulf scholarly bodies reject. This is a real and documented juristic divergence, not a compliance failure in either direction.

phases.name: Doktrin lock
phases.deliverable: Published baseline: current PLS share, tawarruq share, maqasid statement, third-party Shariah audit charter

phases.name: Funding side first
phases.deliverable: Investment accounts (mudarabah/musyarakah) from fringe product to primary funding instrument

phases.name: Asset glide — flagship
phases.deliverable: Home financing: tawarruq to musharakah mutanaqisah on new originations

phases.name: Sector concentration
phases.deliverable: Risk-sharing in long-horizon sectors: halal/food security, waqf property, climate transition

phases.name: Social finance engine
phases.deliverable: Waqf, zakat routing, qardhul hasan, microfinance at regional scale

phases.name: Scale
phases.deliverable: Only now: merger / consolidation on top of a converted model

Shariah committee independence.target: fixed terms, published fatwa rationale, product veto

Shariah non-compliance income.target: disclosed with full routing to qardhul hasan/charity

Qardhul hasan book.target: funded from non-compliance income + fixed profit share

failure_modes.desc: Announced as an Islamic mega-bank; book stays ~90% tawarruq; the label grows and the substance does not.
PLS pilots launched as flagship products while the balance sheet mix is unchanged; no measurable target, no third-party audit.
PLS share rises but capital is not raised; growth stalls and the programme is reversed within two years on ROE grounds.
Shariah committee becomes advisory in form; fatwa rationale unpublished; independent members not renewed.
Funding side converted, home financing migrated, maqasid verified — the bank becomes genuinely different, and smaller-margin.
